Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:10:1.hebrew: אמרי מדנקט תנא - במתני' למילף סימנין משמלה בהדי תובעין, פשיטא ליה דשה למלתא אחריתי אתא, ואנן הוא דלא ידעינן. משום הכי לא פשיטא ליה לקמן סימנין משה, הלכך קשיא לן למאי אתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:10:1.english: They say: Since the Tanna chose - in the Mishnah to derive distinguishing marks from “garment” together with claimants, it is obvious to him that “sheep” comes for another matter, and it is we who do not know [what it is]. Therefore, later on, [deriving] distinguishing marks from “sheep” is not obvious to him; thus it is difficult for us: for what [purpose] does it come?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:11:1.english: Which shall be lost - That it be called a lost item.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:11:2.english: And you have found it - That it should be called a finding.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:14:1.hebrew: דאתא לידיה משמע - ואפילו הכי, "אחיך" — ולא עובד כוכבים, ולמדך שאבידת כנעני מותרת. ולא תימא כי אמעוט אבידת כנעני, מלטרוח אחריה אמעוט, אבל אי נקטה — חייב לאהדורה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:14:1.english: It means that it has come into his hand - And even so, ["your brother's" implies] your brother and not an idolater, and [thus] it teaches you that the lost property of a Canaanite is permitted. And do not say [that] when the lost property of a Canaanite was excluded, it was excluded [only] from troubling oneself [to go] after it, but if he took it, he is obligated to return it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:16:1.english: That which is lost from him - And since [Scripture] wrote "from him," it wrote "which shall be lost."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:17:1.english: And you have found it - The extra vav implies [that] you have already found it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:19:1.hebrew: שהוזלה - דבשעת אבידה שוה פרוט', ובשע' מציאה הוזלה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:19:1.english: That was devalued - That at the time of loss [it was] worth a perutah, and at the time of finding it was devalued.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:1:1.hebrew: בלוקח מן התגר - שאף הוא לקח תבואה זו מאנשים הרבה, ולא ידיע דמאן נינהו, וכיון דלית בהו סימן, נתייאשו הבעלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:1:1.english: In [the case of] one who purchases from a merchant - For he too purchased this grain from many people, and it is not known whose [coins] they are; and since they have no identifying mark, the owners have despaired [of recovering them].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:2:1.hebrew: דשן - וכי הוא עצמו דש את התבואה הזאת? הלא פועלים הרבה דשו אותה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:2:1.english: Threshed them - Did he himself thresh this grain? Did not many laborers thresh it?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:2:2.english: Should I delete it - I will remove this baraita from my version.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:2:3.hebrew: אמר ליה לא תסמי תתרגם מתנית'. כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:2:3.english: He said to him: Do not delete [it]; interpret the Mishnah, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:3:1.english: In the generalization of all these - In the Gemara, [it] explains it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:3:2.hebrew: למה יצאתה - "וכן תעשה לשמלתו": סתם שמלה יש בה סימן, וכל שמלה יש לה בעלים תובעין אותה, שלא נעשית אלא בידי אדם, ולא באת מן ההפקר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:3:2.english: Why did it emerge - [as it states:] "And so shall you do with his garment": An ordinary garment has a distinguishing mark, and every garment has owners who claim it, since it is only made by human hands and does not come from ownerless [property].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:3:3.english: So too any [item] that has claimants - To exclude something regarding which we know that [the owner] has despaired [of recovering it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:5:1.hebrew: שור וחמור שה ושמלה - לא תראה את שור אחיך או שיו, וכן תעשה לחמורו, וכן תעשה לשמלתו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:5:1.english: An ox and a donkey, a sheep and a garment - "You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep ... and so shall you do with his donkey, and so shall you do with his garment."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:6:1.english: By distinguishing marks of a saddle - If he does not have a distinguishing mark on the donkey, but he has a distinguishing mark on the saddle that is upon it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:6:2.english: The Merciful One wrote: "Donkey" - [It is] an extra verse for exposition.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:7:1.hebrew: לגיזת זנבו - שאפי' שער שבסוף הזנב יחזיר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:7:1.english: For the shearing of its tail - That he must return even the hair at the end of the tail.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:8:1.hebrew: חמור דבור לרבי יהודה - דמחייב על נזקי כלים בבור, קשיא לן למאי אתא, דאילו לרבנן מבעי להו שור ולא אדם, חמור ולא כלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:8:1.english: “Donkey” of Pit according to Rabbi Yehuda - Who holds [one] liable for damage to vessels in a pit — it is difficult for us [to know] why [this word] is stated, whereas according to the Rabbis they require [the verse to teach]: “ox” and not a person, “donkey” and not vessels.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:9:1.hebrew: לגללים - להחזיר את גלליו, דאי כתב שור הוה אמינא כי אתא לגיזת זנבו אתא, אבל גללים לא חשיבי ולא ליהדר; כתב רחמנא קרא יתירא לאתויי גללים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:9:1.english: For dung - To return its dung; for had [the Torah] written [only] "ox," I would have said [that] when [the extra term] comes, it comes for the shearings of its tail, whereas dung is not significant and one would not return [it] — [therefore] the Merciful One wrote an extra verse to include dung.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:9:2.hebrew: אפקורי מפקר להו - למי שטרח בו, ולא אתא קרא לרבויינהו, דאין לו תובעין הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:9:2.english: He renounces ownership of them - [Leaving them] to whoever troubled himself with it, and the verse did not come to include them, for it has no claimants.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:9:3.hebrew: לסימנין אתא - לאשמועינן דליהדריה בסימנין בלא עדים, דקמיבעי' לן לקמן: סימנין דאורייתא או דרבנן, ובעינן למפשט ממתניתין דיליף להו משמלה, ודחינן ואמר: תנא תובעין אצטריכא ליה, סימנין כדי נסבה. נפשוט מקרא יתירא דשה לסימנין אתא, וסימנין דאורייתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 27a:9:3.english: It comes for distinguishing marks - To teach us that one should return it based on distinguishing marks without witnesses; for we raise a dilemma later [in the Gemara]: [Are] distinguishing marks [effective] by Torah law or by rabbinic law? And we sought to resolve [it] from our Mishnah, which derives them from "garment," and we rejected [that proof], saying: "The Tanna needed [the verse for] claimants; [mentioning] distinguishing marks was merely incidental." Let us [then] resolve [the dilemma] from the superfluous verse, [concluding] that "sheep" comes for distinguishing marks, and [thus] distinguishing marks are by Torah law.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:11:1.hebrew: פרט לשאין בו שוה פרוטה - דס"ד דחייב מכלל "כל אבידת אחיך":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:11:1.english: To exclude [a lost item] in which there is not the value of a peruta - Because you might have thought that one is obligated [to return it] from the inclusive phrase "every lost item of your brother."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:1:1.hebrew: בלוקח מן התגר - פרש"י שלקח מאנשים הרבה ועירב פירות יחד ואינו יודע של מי הן, ובאין בו סימן מיירי. וא"ת: אמאי לא מוקי בלוקח שהוא תגר? וי"ל: דלא פסיקא ליה, דאם מצא קודם ששהא כדי לערבו בפירות אחרים — חייב להחזיר; אבל בלוקח מן התגר, כבר עירב התגר. ועי"ל: בלא טעם דמערב עם שאר הפירות, "לא שנו אלא בלוקח מן התגר", שאינו יודע למי להחזיר — או לתגר או לבעה"ב; אפי' אם אינו הוה ליפול בתבואה כ"א בשעת דישה ואין להסתפק בתגר, מ"מ אינו יודע מאיזה בעל הבית קנה התגר. ולזה הפי', הו"מ למימר בלוקח שהוא תגר, ומתייאש בעל הבית שסבר שכבר מכר התגר ואין הקונה יודע למי יחזיר; אלא כמו כן, משום דלא פסיקא ליה, דאם התגר מצאה קודם ששהה כדי למכור לאחר — לא נתייאש בעה"ב, וחייב להחזיר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:1:1.english: In [the case of] one who purchases from a merchant - Rashi explained that [the merchant] purchased from many people and mixed [the] produce together, so he does not know whose [coins] they are; and [the Mishnah] is dealing with [coins] that have no identifying mark. And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not establish [the Mishnah] as [referring to] a buyer who is a merchant? One can answer: Because it is not a fixed [rule], for if he found [the coins] before he waited long enough to mix [the produce] with other produce, he would be obligated to return [them]; whereas in [the case of] one who purchases from a merchant, the merchant has already mixed [them]. And one can also answer: Even without the reason of mixing with other produce, "[the Sages] taught [this] only in [the case of] one who purchases from a merchant" because he does not know to whom to return [the coins] — whether to the merchant or to the owner; even if [coins] only tend to fall into grain at the time of threshing and there is no doubt regarding the merchant, nevertheless he does not know from which owner the merchant bought [the grain]. And according to this explanation, [the Gemara] could have said [that the Mishnah refers to] a buyer who is a merchant, and the owner despairs [of recovering the coins] because he assumes that the merchant has already sold [the produce] and the buyer does not know to whom to return [them]; rather, similarly, [it did not say so] because it is not a fixed [rule], for if the merchant found [the coins] before he waited long enough to sell [the produce] to another, the owner has not despaired and [the merchant] is obligated to return [them].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:3:1.hebrew: מה שמלה מיוחדת שיש לה סימני' ויש לה תובעין - במרובה (ב"ק דף סו. ושם ד"ה מוצא) אמרינן: בגניבה ילפינן יאוש מאבידה. וא"ת: ואבידה גופה מנלן? וי"ל, דמהכא נפקא לן: דמה שמלה מיוחדת שיש בה סימן ואין הבעלים מתייאשין, אלא תובעין שיחזירוה להם בסימנין; אפי' אי סימנין לאו דאורייתא ואין מחזירין אלא בעדים, מ"מ ילפינן משמלה דדווקא דבר שיש בו סימן חייב להחזיר, דע"י שיש בו סימן ימצא עדים, שיאמר להם: "מכירים אתם שמלה שלי שהיו בה סימנין כך וכך?", וגם המוצא לא יוציא השמלה להראותה לכל אדם, אלא למי שיתן בה סימנים — אע"פ שאינו מחזירה לו בכך, מ"מ דומה שהיא שלו ומראה אותה לעדים — אבל דברים שאין בהן סימן הוי שלו, לפי שהבעלים נתייאשו. והא דקאמר בגמרא: "סימנין כדי נסבה", אע"ג דצריך הסימנין דע"י זה יש לה תובעין, מ"מ כדי נסבה, דאפילו אי לא תני אלא "שיש לה תובעין", מ"מ ידעינן דע"י סימנין יש לה תובעין ואין הבעלים מתייאשים, כדפרישית. ומיהו בירושלמי יליף: מניין ליאוש מן התורה? אמר רבי יוחנן: "אשר תאבד ממנו" — מי שאבודה ממנו ומצויה אצל כל אדם, יצאה זו כו':
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:3:1.english: "What [is notable about] a garment? [It is notable] in that it has distinguishing marks and it has claimants" - In [the chapter] Merubah (Bava Kamma 66a, and ibid., s.v. motzei) [the Gemara] says: Regarding theft, we derive [the law of] despair from [the law of] a lost item. And if you will say: And from where do we [know the law of despair regarding] a lost item itself? And one can answer that it is derived from here: just as a garment is notable in that it has a distinguishing mark and the owners do not despair [of recovering it], rather they claim [it] so that [the finders] will return it to them through distinguishing marks; even if distinguishing marks are not [valid] by Torah law and one may only return [a lost item] with witnesses, nevertheless we derive from "garment" that specifically an item that has a distinguishing mark one is obligated to return, because through its having a distinguishing mark [the owner] will find witnesses, as he will say to them: "Do you recognize my garment that had such-and-such distinguishing marks?" And furthermore, the finder will not take out the garment to show it to just anyone, only to one who gives distinguishing marks for it — even though he does not return it to him on that basis, nevertheless it appears that it is his, and he shows it to [his] witnesses — whereas items that do not have a distinguishing mark belong to [the finder], because the owners have despaired [of recovering them]. And as for what [the Gemara] says: "[The mention of] distinguishing marks is mentioned incidentally," even though distinguishing marks are needed because through this it has claimants, nevertheless it is mentioned incidentally, for even if [the Mishnah] had only taught "that it has claimants," we would still know that it is through distinguishing marks that it has claimants and the owners do not despair, as I have explained. However, in the [Talmud] Yerushalmi it derives [it differently]: From where [is] despair [derived] from the Torah? Rabbi Yochanan said: "[which] shall be lost from him" (Deuteronomy 22:3) — [this applies to] that which is lost from him and available to everyone; excluded is this [case], etc.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:6:1.hebrew: בעדי אוכף - פי': אי סימנין לאו דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:6:1.english: With witnesses of [the] saddle - Explanation: [this is] if distinguishing marks are not by Torah law.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:7:1.hebrew: לגיזת זנבו - וא"ת: אם יש בה שוה פרוטה, פשיטא; ואם אין בה שוה פרוטה, הא ממעטינן לקמן מהשבה? וי"ל: דאצטריך שחייב לגוזזה בעתה, אע"פ שאין בה שוה פרוטה בשעה שגזזה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:7:1.english: For the shearing of its tail - And if you will ask: If it has the value of a perutah, it is obvious [that one must return it]; and if it does not have the value of a perutah, behold, we exclude [less than a perutah] later on from [the term] "returning"? And one can answer: It is necessary [to teach] that he is obligated to shear it in its [proper] time, even though it does not have the value of a perutah at the time that he shears it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:8:1.hebrew: חמור דבור לרבי יהודה - הא דלא קאמר גם לב"ה קשה, דלא חשיב אלא בהמות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:8:1.english: "Donkey" [stated] with regard to Pit, according to Rabbi Yehuda - [The reason the Gemara] does not say "it is also difficult according to Beit Hillel" [is] because it only lists animals:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:8:2.hebrew: ושה דאבידה לדברי הכל קשיא - מקשינן: ונימא מלתא דאתיא בק"ו טרח וכתב לה קרא? ותירץ הר"י כהן, דכיון דנכתב "שור" לגיזת זנבו, הוי גיזת שה בכלל "כל אבידת אחיך":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 27a:8:2.english: And [the term] “sheep” [stated] with regard to a lost item, according to everyone, is difficult - We ask: Why should we not say [that this is] a matter that is derived through an a fortiori inference (kal vachomer), [which] Scripture took the trouble to write explicitly? And R. Yitzchak Kohen answered that since “ox” was written for the shearings of its tail, the shearings of a sheep are [already] included in [the phrase] “every lost item of your brother.”
